newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: No progress seen in Philippines budget impasse.
newsitem.headline: No progress seen in Philippines budget impasse.

text.p: The Philippine Senate and the Lower House held on Monday the first of two special sessions to hammer out their differences over the 1997 budget but little progress is likely, Congress officials said.
They said the most the two can do is pass two special appropriation bills should the stalemate continue.

The House of Representatives said it passed on Monday a bill on salary increases for government employees worth 27 billion pesos and the additional internal revenue allocation of local government units for 14 billion pesos. The Senate said it expects to pass these two measures on Tuesday.

"We will not be able to approve the budget in two days. So we will only be able to approve the two bills to ensure that salary increases will be granted by January 1 and that increases in the internal revenue allocation will be approved," said Senator Ernesto Herrera, the Senate Finance Committee chairman.
"Somebody will have to blink first," he said, adding that the House would have to agree to a cut in the countrywide development fund (CDF), which has divided the two sides.

The two had come to a deadlock after the opposition-dominated Senate slashed the CDF by 40 percent to 720 million pesos. Senators said they feared the fund would be used by the administration-backed Lower House for early campaigning ahead of the presidential and congressional elections in May 1998.
House members have said the Senate does not have the constitutional right to amend its proposals.

Failure of the special sessions to pass the 1997 budget will not paralyse the operations of the government. Under Philippine law, it can draw money on the basis of the previous budget until Congress approves a new one.
But provisions for the CDF and other special funds will not be covered under the old budget, for which an agreement between the two wings of Congress will be needed.
